title: Mandodarī mourns Rāvaṇa
voice: Mandodarī speaks after seeing Rāvaṇa killed.
summary: She recalls the ruler’s extraordinary power and asks how a man who lived in the forest could bring him down. Her words give the defeated household a voice after the battle.
aftermath: The chapter turns from lament to the rites for the dead. Laṅkā will face the question of rule under Vibhīṣaṇa.

title: Bharata returns authority
voice: Bharata addresses Rāma after his return.
summary: Bharata gives the kingdom back. He compares the task of carrying it alone to a young animal struggling with the heavy load of a stronger one.
aftermath: The return closes the succession conflict at the end of Yuddha. The earlier unease about what a king owes the household and city continues in Uttara.

title: Vālmīki names Sītā’s twins
voice: The young people of the hermitage tell Vālmīki that Sītā has given birth.
summary: The sage uses kuśa grass and blade cuttings in a protective rite and names the twins Kuśa and Lava. The account explains the names through the items used in the rite.
aftermath: The children grow up away from the court. Their later presence reconnects the events of the hermitage to the royal gathering.

title: Vālmīki’s question
voice: Vālmīki asks Nārada about a person whose conduct is worth knowing.
summary: The poem opens with a question about virtue, courage and truthful conduct. Nārada answers by naming Rāma and gives a short account of the story before it unfolds at length.
aftermath: The first chapter anticipates later events. It is a narrative frame rather than the first stop on Rāma’s journey.

title: The birth of the princes
voice: The narrator introduces the sons of Daśaratha.
summary: Kauśalyā bears Rāma. The Baroda main text gives a brief birth description at this point. The Southern Recension preserves a longer birth passage with Caitra Navamī and a reference to Aditi’s asterism.
aftermath: The separate birth lesson lets readers compare the witnesses and see why a calendar tradition needs a stated textual basis.

title: Janaka tells where Sītā came from
voice: Janaka recounts what happened while preparing a field.
summary: As Janaka ploughs the ground he finds a girl. His account connects her name with the furrow and sets up the conditions he lays down for her marriage.
aftermath: This is Sītā’s origin as Janaka narrates it. She later invokes the earth at the gathering in Uttara.

title: Janaka joins the households
voice: Janaka addresses the princes at the marriage.
summary: Janaka offers Sītā to Rāma and directs the joining of hands. The marriage passage also joins the other princes and brides of the two households.
aftermath: The royal kinship sets the background for Sītā’s decision whether to accompany Rāma into exile.

title: The coronation becomes exile
voice: Kaikeyī explains the old promise to Rāma.
summary: Kaikeyī uses two saved boons to seek Bharata’s installation and Rāma’s departure to the forest for fourteen years. Rāma agrees to go in order to keep Daśaratha’s word.
aftermath: This creates a succession crisis and leaves several members of the household to decide what loyalty requires.

title: Sītā chooses to go
voice: Sītā replies to Rāma in Ayodhyā.
summary: Rāma has explained why she should remain in the city. Sītā answers that the circumstances of a wife are bound to those of her husband and treats his exile as hers too.
aftermath: The warning about forest life continues in the next chapter. Sītā contests it again at 2.26–27.

title: Rāma lists the risks of the forest
voice: Rāma asks Sītā to reconsider.
summary: He tells her that the forest brings hardship and makes a case for her staying behind. His appeal puts everyday conditions, not simply court protocol, into the discussion.
aftermath: Sītā answers that his account of hardship does not change her choice.

title: Crossing the Gaṅgā
voice: Rāma speaks to Lakṣmaṇa as the party reaches the water.
summary: The three cross the river during the departure from Kosala. Sītā addresses the river on the crossing. The chapter records a journey stage, with routes still uncertain in modern geography.
aftermath: The river marks a transition away from the royal household. The exiles continue to Citrakūṭa.

title: Bharata takes the sandals
voice: Bharata requests a token from Rāma.
summary: Bharata asks Rāma to step into the sandals, then receives them. The reunion does not persuade Rāma to end his father’s promised term of exile.
aftermath: Bharata takes the sandals as a sign of the elder brother’s authority and returns without him.

title: Making a home in Pañcavaṭī
voice: Rāma addresses Lakṣmaṇa as the three arrive.
summary: Rāma identifies the wooded place and asks Lakṣmaṇa to select ground for a dwelling. The account describes a living place in the forest, before it becomes the scene of separation.
aftermath: The later association with present-day Nashik is a pilgrimage tradition. The verse supplies no modern coordinates.

title: Rāvaṇa reveals his disguise
voice: Rāvaṇa speaks to Sītā, who calls out as he takes her.
summary: Rāvaṇa abandons the guise of an ascetic, seizes Sītā and places her in his vehicle. She calls to those who might hear and names the place she is being taken from.
aftermath: Her cries draw Jaṭāyu into the conflict at the beginning of the next sarga.

title: Jaṭāyu confronts Rāvaṇa
voice: Jaṭāyu answers Sītā’s cry and addresses Rāvaṇa.
summary: The great bird wakes, names himself and challenges the attempt to take Sītā. His intervention turns the abduction into a fight that the searchers will learn about afterward.
aftermath: The incident supplies a witness to the departure, but no measurable itinerary across the landscape.

title: Hanumān speaks to the strangers
voice: Hanumān approaches Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa for Sugrīva.
summary: Hanumān is sent to find out who has arrived. He introduces himself after speaking with the two exiles. Their meeting creates a way to negotiate with Sugrīva.
aftermath: The contact becomes an alliance with its own obligations in the following chapters.

title: Rāma and Sugrīva make an alliance
voice: Sugrīva offers friendship. Hanumān prepares a fire.
summary: Sugrīva extends his hand. The two walk around the fire to seal their bond. Each needs help that the other can offer.
aftermath: Their bargain leads to the confrontation with Vāli before the search is fully under way.

title: Vāli asks who can punish him
voice: The wounded Vāli challenges Rāma about the shot.
summary: Vāli asks why Rāma struck him when he was fighting somebody else. He questions the ruler’s jurisdiction and whether outward signs of virtue match this act.
aftermath: Rāma responds in the next sarga. Keeping the two speeches separate preserves the disagreement.

title: Rāma answers Vāli
voice: Rāma replies to Vāli’s accusations.
summary: He invokes the ruler’s power to punish wrongdoing and characterizes Vāli’s conduct toward his brother’s household as a violation. His argument depends on authority that Vāli had questioned.
aftermath: The answer leaves the reader with both positions. The death changes who can rule Kiṣkindhā and carry out the alliance.

title: Hanumān takes the sea crossing
voice: The narrator follows Hanumān as he begins the task.
summary: Hanumān prepares to cross the sea to look for Sītā. The search that had stopped at the shore becomes a single messenger’s journey.
aftermath: The crossing is a literary action and stays separate from Nala’s later bridge in the war book.

title: Hanumān enters the Aśoka grove
voice: Hanumān searches the landscape inside Laṅkā.
summary: He examines the grove and the surroundings in which he hopes to find the captive. The description gives the reader a setting for the later meeting.
aftermath: The grove is a named literary setting. The atlas leaves its modern coordinates open.

title: Sītā recognizes the ring
voice: Hanumān offers the ring. Sītā asks about allies and preparations.
summary: Hanumān shows Rāma’s inscribed ring. Sītā questions him about Rāma’s safety and whether he is taking steps to gain help.
aftermath: The token gives grounds for trust, and Sītā’s words reveal that the rescue depends on an alliance and a plan.

title: The sky described during the march
voice: The campaign narrative includes a description of the sky.
summary: The passage names Brahmarāśi among other sky markers. Oak identifies it with Vega. The identity and a tolerable angular distance from the pole are questions a model must state explicitly.
aftermath: The pole comparison shows how the geometry changes with epoch. It does not assign any time to an event in the story.

title: Rāma decides whether to grant shelter
voice: Rāma tells the allies how he will treat an appeal for refuge.
summary: Vibhīṣaṇa’s break with his brother Rāvaṇa makes the allies consider whether they can trust him. Rāma states a rule of accepting someone who comes seeking protection.
aftermath: Rāma’s decision adds a member of Laṅkā’s own ruling house to the coalition.

title: Nala leads the crossing work
voice: The ocean proposes Nala as builder. The narration describes the bridge.
summary: Nala organizes the work and the force reaches the far shore. The story uses a comparison with a line through the sea to describe the completed crossing.
aftermath: The question of a modern shoal’s depth and shape belongs to remote sensing. That measurement cannot date the narrated construction.

title: Sītā answers after the battle
voice: Sītā speaks and enters the fire after Rāma’s public challenge.
summary: With Rāvaṇa defeated, the reunion becomes a public questioning of Sītā. She calls on the fire as witness to her conduct and enters it. The people watching witness her choice.
aftermath: The scene continues into the gods’ and Agni’s responses. Uttara returns to the question of how a ruler responds to public suspicion.

title: The return looks back across the sea
voice: Rāma speaks to Sītā on the way back.
summary: The homeward passage names the bridge and points out places connected with the campaign. It recounts stages from the route after the fighting has ended.
aftermath: This is a remembered itinerary within the narrative, and its connection to any modern route needs separate evidence.

title: Rāma orders a second exile
voice: Rāma instructs Lakṣmaṇa after hearing reports from the city.
summary: He fears continuing public reproach and orders Lakṣmaṇa to take Sītā beyond the realm and leave her near Vālmīki’s hermitage. Sītā is given no voice in the order.
aftermath: The account examines the burden of royal reputation through a decision that costs Sītā her place at court. Later chapters give her words in public.

title: Sītā calls on the earth
voice: Sītā speaks for herself before the gathered company.
summary: Sītā declares her fidelity and asks the earth to receive her. The narration then describes a throne rising from the ground.
aftermath: The episode recalls the furrow in Janaka’s account of her origin. It belongs to the Uttara book of the edition and has its own reception history.
